speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing this chronic cough and recurrent bouts of bronchitis? Do you have a history of smoking or exposure to occupational dusts or chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience shortness of breath or wheezing, and do you have any family history of cystic fibrosis or early-onset lung disease? I would also like to know if you have noticed any nasal congestion or sinus issues that persist throughout the year.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of chronic sinusitis or nasal polyps, and do you experience shortness of breath or wheezing? REQUEST TEST: Chest_CT_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of chronic sinusitis or nasal polyps? I would like to check for other signs of cystic fibrosis or primary ciliary dyskinesia. REQUEST TEST: Sweat_Chloride_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal chest CT and sweat chloride test, I suspect Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia. Do you have a history of chronic otitis media or hearing loss, and did you have respiratory issues as an infant? REQUEST TEST: Nasal_Nitric_Oxide

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal nasal nitric oxide level makes Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia unlikely. Given the copious purulent sputum and recurrent infections despite a normal CT, I suspect a localized issue like a broncholith or retained foreign body. REQUEST TEST: Bronchoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the bronchoscopy was normal, I need to rule out structural airway abnormalities that might not be fully captured by a standard CT. Do you experience any episodes of sudden coughing fits or wheezing that resolve spontaneously, suggesting airway collapse? REQUEST TEST: Bronchial_Dilometry
